findings.title: Shard-splitting path now interpolates every target twice
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() now maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() (line 52), but the already-interpolated targets are then passed via subRequest into runSplitQuery() (line 163), which after this PR also maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() (querySplitting.ts line 299). So in the shard path each query is interpolated once per shard-group request plus once at entry. The updated test codifies this: 'Interpolates queries before running' now expects applyTemplateVariables to have been called 5 times for a single-target request (1 + 4 shard sub-requests). Re-running template expansion on already-interpolated text is a known source of query corruption in Grafana: if a variable's value contains '$'-syntax (e.g. a custom variable value containing '${other_var}' or a label value with a '$' token matching another variable), the second pass will expand tokens introduced by the first pass and silently change the query sent to Loki. Additionally, because subRequest spreads the original request, request.filters survives into runSplitQuery, so ad hoc filters are injected into the selector twice (once per interpolation pass), producing duplicated matchers in the generated LogQL. Consider interpolating only once, e.g. by having runShardSplitQuery pass a flag so runSplitQuery skips interpolation for already-interpolated sub-requests.

findings.title: Empty-expr filter now runs before interpolation instead of after
findings.body: Before this change, the shard path interpolated first (datasource.interpolateVariablesInQueries) and then filtered out queries with an empty expr, so a query whose expr was only a variable that expands to an empty string was dropped. The new code filters on the raw, uninterpolated expr (lines 50-51) and interpolates afterwards (line 52), so such a query now passes the filter and proceeds with an empty interpolated expr: it is grouped via getSelectorForShardValues(''), triggers a fetchLabelValues call with an empty stream selector, and is ultimately sent to Loki as an empty query, which will return a parse error to the user instead of being silently ignored. The same ordering exists in the updated runSplitQuery (querySplitting.ts lines 296-299). Move the empty-expr check to after the applyTemplateVariables map, or filter again after interpolation.
